newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania maize, beet, oilseed sowings satisfactory.
newsitem.headline: Romania maize, beet, oilseed sowings satisfactory.

text.p: Romania's farmers have made good progress with sowing of all crop, including maize, sugar beet and sunflowers, a farm ministry official said on Wednesday.
"The present pace of sowing is satisfactory for all crops," the official said without elaborating.
Maize sowing was complete on 1.93 million hectares, a 20 percent increase over the past five days.
"There are still some 1.19 million hectares left to be put under maize. We hope to complete this operation by the end of this week provided the weather stays fine," the official said.
Last Friday, ministry data showed maize had been sown on 41 percent of the planned area of 3.13 million.
The official said sunflowers had been sown on 636,441 ha of the planned 781,822, or 16 percent up since last Friday.
Sugar beet sowing on the planned 138,401 ha was almost complete, with ministry data showing some 126,375 ha, or 91 percent of the planned area, already under that crop.

Minstry data on Wednesday also said herbicides had been spread on 1.27 million hectares of wheat, or 53 percent of the 2.37 million ha planted last autumn. This compared to 41 percent recorded last Friday.

Last week, the ministry forecast a bumper wheat crop of around 7.8 million tonnes and exports amounting to some 1.5 million tonnes this year, which could bring Romania back among the major players on the world grain market.

Heavy rainfall last month delayed farm work, hitting sowing of maize, sugar beet and sunflowers. Reports said high soil humidity had favoured the growth of weeds on large areas. --Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
